paper_title: From Zero to Hero Harnessing Transformers for Biomedical Named Entity   Recognition in Zero- and Few-shot Contexts
caption: : Caption not extracted
model_annotation: The pie chart summarizes the distribution of named-entity categories in a biomedical NER setting, showing 26 labeled slices with category names placed around the perimeter and percentage values printed inside most segments (there is no separate legend and no slices appear exploded or otherwise emphasized). The largest slice is labeled “Chemical” and is colored deep blue at approximately 32%, followed by “Protein” in orange at about 15% and “DNA” in green at about 6%. Three similarly sized mid-range slices—“Chemical Family” (red), “Disease” (purple), and “Cell Type” (brown)—are each shown at roughly 5%, and “Drug” (pink) is about 4%. Three adjacent smaller slices—“Frequency” (gray), “Cell Line” (yellow), “Dosage” (light blue), and “Strength” (dark blue)—are each approximately 3%. Several additional categories appear as thin slices in a variety of distinct colors, including “Gene Or Gene Product,” “Form,” “Disease Or Phenotypic Feature,” “Specific Disease,” “Reason,” and “Route,” each shown at roughly 2%, and a set of very small slices labeled “Chemical Entity,” “Sequence Variant,” “Modifier,” “No label,” “RNA,” “Disease Class,” “Organism Taxon,” “Duration,” and “Composite Mention,” each around ~1% or less (some labels appear to round to 0–1%). Visually, the slices appear arranged roughly from larger segments on the left/top toward many progressively thinner segments clustered on the right side.
